full_judgment:
14. Mr.Kazi Shahadat Hossain, learned Advocate for the plaintiff opposite party, does not contest the proposition of law advanced by the learned Advocate for the petitioner. He, however, submits that the suit filed by the plaintiff-opposite party is not a suit to enforce the award at all He has vehemently argued that this is an independent suit for determination of damages by the Court afresh on the basis of independent evidence to be led by the respective parties in the Court itself and it is a suit for a decree for damages after determination thereof. This is also a suit not limited to the amount awarded by the Arbitrator. Additionally, the plaintiff prays for interest which the Arbitrator did not give. Mr. Kazi Shahadat Hossain submits that such a suit is not barred by section 32 of the Arbitration Act. He submits that the award has died a natural death because none of the parties enforced it by making it a rule of the Court within the period of limitation. The plaintiff-opposite party has stated the facts about the award, not because the plaintiff wants on enforce the award but because the facts that occurred had to be stated from the beginning to the end. The plaintiffs did not file any suit for enforcing any award at all and so the aforesaid decisions do not apply. 

 16. The award is therefore not a mere sequence in the narration of events. It is the basis of the plaintiffs claim against the defendant Mr. Kazi Shahadat Hossain submits that this is an independent suit for determination of damages. It is in the plaint that the defendant-petitioner took delivery of the plaintiffs oil tanker in the middle of October, 1969 for repairs with a promise to rearm the vessel within 5 weeks thereof after complete repairs. Under Article 65 of the Limitation Act a suit for compensation for breach of a promise to do anything at a specified time, or upon the happening of a specified contingency is to be filed within 3 years from the period when the time specified arrives or the contingency happens. If it was an independent suit for damages then the plaintiff-opposite party could have traced back its cause of action from the middle of October, 1969. Nothing has been stated in the plaint as to why the amount of compensation should be Tk. 4,43,636.18, not a paisa more or less than the award given by the Arbitrator and how the said amount has been calculated.
